sections.title: The letter G
paragraphs: You call this letter (G) /dʒ/. Its main sound is a consonant in the word (gas) /ɡæs/, which means a form of matter like air. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth blocks or narrows the air. This letter makes four different sounds in English.

sections.title: How to speak it
paragraphs: For the first sound, raise the back of your tongue to touch the roof of your mouth. Stop the air, then let it burst out with your voice. For the second sound, press your tongue tip behind your teeth and release a voiced hiss. For the third sound, blow air through your tongue and teeth smoothly. For the last sound, keep your mouth quiet.

sections.title: When to use each
paragraphs: Before the vowels a, o, u or before consonants, say it as in (gas) /ɡæs/. Often before the vowels e, i or y, say it as in (gem) /dʒɛm/. In words from French, say it as in (genre) /ʒɑn.rə/. Sometimes the letter is a silent letter, where you do not pronounce it at all before n, as in (gnat) /næt/ or (sign) /saɪn/.

sections.title: Mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not confuse the hard sound with the soft sound. Learners often say the sound from (gem) /dʒɛm/ when they read words like (gap) /ɡæp/. Always check the vowel that follows the letter. Also, remember not to pronounce the letter at all in words like (gnat) /næt/.
